clue.text: Spirit trains boy

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the old national train operator
Andy is a common boy's name

explanation.surface: Liquor is what is training a lad, or a ghost drilling a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled liquor, and spirit is the general term for such strong drink.

clue.text: They were used instead of aprons by printers in Geneva

definitions.text: They were used instead of aprons by printers in Geneva

parts.words: They were used instead of aprons by printers in Geneva
parts.note: the Geneva Bible of 1560 has Adam and Eve sew fig leaves into a pair of legwear rather than aprons, giving that edition its nickname

explanation.surface: Swiss printers wore something other than aprons at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The printers seem to wear the garment; really it is the word printed in Genesis 3:7.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Geneva Bible translates the fig-leaf garments as knee-length trousers, hence the famous nickname.

clue.text: Firm employing Scottish architect, an industrious worker

parts.note: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish architect
the ant is proverbially hard-working

explanation.surface: A company hires a Scottish designer and a diligent employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding, resolute and unshakeable.

clue.text: Understand, I can accept a pound for a drug

parts.note: dig is slang for understand

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a tin is a can
L is the symbol for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone saying they get it and will take a pound in exchange for medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalin is a heart stimulant drawn from foxglove.

clue.text: Two spirits fancy a game

parts.note: gin and rum are two kinds of strong liquor
the second of the two liquors
'Fancy!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A pair of liquors imagine some contest to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like a verb or an adjective, but it is the exclamation 'Fancy (that)!', which equals 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-player card game of melds, named for the two drinks in its title.

clue.text: Remind cabin boy to repair lighter

indicators.note: to repair is to put back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Tell the ship's lad to fix a cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' looks like a cigarette lighter; it is something that sets fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raising device dropped from aircraft is literally something that lights.

clue.text: Run over pedestrian on the way north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pacer is one who walks at a measured pace

explanation.surface: Knock down someone walking along a road heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' suggests a traffic accident, but it means to summarise.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again.

clue.text: Scholar with books about barbarian's criminal pursuit

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a scholar

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
the Huns were barbarian invaders

explanation.surface: An academic with volumes on a savage's life of crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhunt is an organised search for a fugitive wanted for a crime.

clue.text: American pulled up with a jerk?

definitions.meaning: a person from the United States
a playful coinage: someone on the receiving end of a sharp tug

explanation.surface: An American stopped short with a sudden tug.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee is a person from the United States; jocularly, one who has been jerked, like an employee is one employed.

clue.text: Mouse died — girl makes a bloomer

parts.note: a mouse is slang for a bruised eye
Susan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A rodent dies and a girl blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-eyed Susan is a flowering plant, and a bloomer is something that flowers.

clue.text: Protestant church suffers setback, without nonconformist leaving

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the church letters go around the rest
to suffer a setback is to be pushed back, so the letters for church are turned round

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: a nonconformist does not keep to the usual order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Protestant congregation hits a snag when a Dissenter departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonconformist leaving' looks like a dissenter departing, but 'nonconformist' is the anagram signal: VANGELI from LEAVING sits inside EC, CE turned round by 'suffers setback', with 'without' meaning outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic is an old form of evangelical, describing the gospel-centred wing of Protestant Christianity.

clue.text: Against accepting an ecclesiastical decree

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Opposing the adoption of a church ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a law laid down by a church council.

clue.text: Coach — it's broken down, out of order

indicators.note: something broken down is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: it, with the 's standing for is as a link

explanation.surface: Complaint that the bus has failed and is out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' reads as the coach being out of service, but here it means in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaotic and out of order both describe things in a state of disarray.

clue.text: God about to write a melody

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for write is read backwards

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A deity is on the point of composing a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the reversal signal on PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman deity of the sea.

clue.text: Celebrate being included in the next Olympics

indicators.note: the answer is included among the letters of the following words, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: Praise taking part in the coming Games.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, which is a way of celebrating someone.

clue.text: Leave the country, settling finally in Islamic territory

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an emirate is a state ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word settling

explanation.surface: Moving abroad, ending up in a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to depart one's homeland to settle abroad.

clue.text: Manoeuvre into anchorage for repairs that may cause delay

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: roads, or roadstead, is a sheltered anchorage
to work a ship is to manoeuvre it

explanation.surface: Steering into harbour for fixes that might hold things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Roads is a nautical term for a sheltered anchorage offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to the highway are notorious for causing traffic hold-ups.

clue.text: Equine complaint causes consternation

definitions.meaning: a disease of horses causing a lurching gait

explanation.surface: A horse illness is alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease of horses that makes them stumble shares its name with a verb for astonishing or bewildering.

clue.text: Animal finding precious water first, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken and the answer sounds like them

parts.note: precious is dear and water is rain, with rain put first: rain-dear

explanation.surface: A creature that seeks out valuable water before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water first' tells you RAIN comes before DEAR (precious) in the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer is an Arctic deer, a large animal herded in Lapland.

clue.text: Avenger crashed in chase

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An avenger smashes up in a pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chase' looks like a pursuit, but it is the metalworker's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase metal is to decorate it by cutting into the surface.

clue.text: A way to hold a business meeting

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
Co is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A method of arranging a commercial get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, and a race meeting there is simply Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the name of an annual English horse-racing fixture, and a racing fixture is called a meeting.

clue.text: In the country, women start to gossip and chat

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: China is a country

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of gossip

explanation.surface: Out in the countryside, women begin gossiping and chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like rural land, but it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal talk.

clue.text: Bay where Herbert in the end turned up

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: end, taken as it stands
APH, the initials of A. P. Herbert, humorist and MP

explanation.surface: Where in the bay did Herbert finally appear?
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the nymph was turned into a bay laurel to escape Apollo.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph of myth became a laurel, the bay tree, and the name is also given to a shrub.

clue.text: In service — one who backs out of service

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a stage show
U/S is short for unserviceable, out of service

explanation.surface: During worship, someone who withdraws from worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs out' looks like withdrawing, but 'one who backs' is the theatrical investor and 'out of service' the abbreviation US.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion recited at set hours, a prayer said in worship.

clue.text: Save a parking place

explanation.surface: Keep a spot for parking.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay by is to put aside for later; a lay-by is a roadside pull-in.

clue.text: Tom is on

parts.note: completes the name of the drowned sailor in Dibdin's sea song 'Tom ...', and in cricket a player who is 'on' is delivering the overs from his end

explanation.definitionFit: The cricketer who is on is sending down deliveries, and the word also completes the title of an old sea song.

clue.text: Exciting dance interrupted by commercial

indicators.note: interrupted by means the second piece breaks into the first

parts.note: the hey is an old country dance with weaving figures
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A thrilling dance spoiled by an advert break.
explanation.definitionFit: Heady means intoxicating or thrilling, much like exciting.

clue.text: New-fangled bras women wear, having support across the chest

definitions.text: wear, having support across the chest

indicators.note: new-fangled means made in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Modern brassieres that ladies put on, giving uplift across the bust.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about bras, but the answer is a military belt with a strap over the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is an officer's belt with a diagonal strap passing over the shoulder and chest.

clue.text: All night Sussex town carries on

parts.note: eve means the night before, as in Christmas Eve

indicators.note: carries means holds, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Rye is a small historic town in East Sussex, England

explanation.surface: A whole night of continuing activity in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries on' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'carries' is the container and 'on' its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone and all both mean every person.

clue.text: Rebuffed, for instance, when interfering in country's traditions

indicators.note: interfering in means getting inside, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: USA's, the possessive of the abbreviation for the United States

indicators.note: rebuffed means sent back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Snubbed, perhaps, for meddling in a nation's customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; GE, EG turned round, goes into USAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are customary practices, which is what traditions are.
